title: Things you should judge employers on
description:
It’s not just them judging you—you’ve got every right to judge them too. Here are the things YOU should be evaluating when considering a job. Remember, it’s a two-way street!  #jobsearchtips #jobsearch

transcript: as a job Seeker here are things that you can and should be judging employers on in this job market it may be easy to forget that interviewing is actually a two-way street and you should be judging if this company is a right fit for you just as hard as they're judging you the first thing that you can judge is that job description do they have a bunch of phrases and words and bullet points in there that actually don't make sense or does it sound like you're going to be doing three jobs in one then stay away from there the second is going to be communication and let's start with the recruiter is the recruiter being timely when they're responding back to you yes then maybe this is a company that values communication if not then maybe it's a company that doesn't and not just thinking about the interview process but do you want to be a part of a company where they don't even communicate with their potential employees now let's talk about the interview process is it a chaotic logistical nightmare are there way too many steps does it take 6 months to make a decision do you want to be at a company where it takes 6 months to make a decision probably not how engaged are the interviewers with you during the interview if interviewers are acting very disengaged they're not interested or they're feeling very rushed it could probably tell you a lot about that culture do you want to be a part of a company that's so chaotic and so busy that you can't even take 30 45 minutes to focus on one task at a time which is interviewing probably not this might just be me but salary transparency is extremely important to me so if you don't have their salary posted on the job description I just feel like you're going to be really difficult when it comes to money and I don't really like that
